title: Kernels of quasi-coherent modules on the small etale site of a scheme
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(u:U\to T)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] such that $M$ and $N$ are quasi-coherent in the sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Then the kernel $\ker\varphi$ in the category of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules, given on each object $U$ of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ by $(\ker\varphi)(U)=\ker(\varphi_U:M(U)\to N(U))$, is quasi-coherent in the sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 0GNB (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), part (3), and its proof via Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), parts (1) and (5): F -> F^a is fully faithful and exact into Mod(S_etale, O). Algebraic-space version: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (3).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], choose quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-modules $F,G$ and isomorphisms $F_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq M$, $G_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq N$. Full faithfulness gives a morphism $\psi:F\to G$ whose associated morphism corresponds to $\varphi$. The morphism formula in [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections] identifies its component at $u:U\to T$ with $\Gamma(U,u^*\psi)$. Thus it suffices to identify the kernel of $\psi_{\mathrm{et}}$; conjugating by the chosen isomorphisms gives the kernel of $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0GNB (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), proof of (3): write a = b^a; Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), (2), and Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites).

proof.text: Form the Zariski module kernel $i:K=\ker\psi\to F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], $K$ is quasi-coherent. The same equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] therefore makes $K_{\mathrm{et}}$ a quasi-coherent module on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Applying the association to $i$ gives a morphism $i_{\mathrm{et}}:K_{\mathrm{et}}\to F_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0GNB (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), proof of (3); Zariski kernel closure is schemes.tex Tag 01LB (item-kernel), affine case Tag 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: Fix any object $u:U\to T$ of the small etale site. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is flat; by [def-weil-flat-morphism] every stalk map $\mathcal O_{T,u(x)}\to\mathcal O_{U,x}$ is flat. Use the tensor pullback $P=u^*$ of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], with its specified action $h\mapsto 1\otimes u^{-1}h$. This action is additive: on a local tensor $b\otimes m$, the map for $h+h'$ sends it to $b\otimes(h(m)+h'(m))=b\otimes h(m)+b\otimes h'(m)$, and the map for zero is zero. The object and map formulas are exactly those required by [lem-sc-stalk-flat-tensor-pullback-kernels], which shows that $u^*i$ is a kernel of $u^*\psi$. Now [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact], applied to the scheme $U$, shows that $\Gamma(U,u^*i)$ identifies $\Gamma(U,u^*K)$ with $\ker(\Gamma(U,u^*\psi))$. This uses preservation of kernels only; global sections need not preserve epimorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), proof of (5), left exactness because etale morphisms are flat; morphisms.tex lemma-etale-flat; modules.tex Tag 01AH (lemma-limits-colimits), (1).

proof.text: By Step 1 and the same morphism formula applied to $i$, the component of $i_{\mathrm{et}}$ at $U$ is precisely the map $\Gamma(U,u^*i)$ of Step 3. Hence $i_{\mathrm{et}}$ is injective on each object and its image there is $\ker((\psi_{\mathrm{et}})_U)$. The sectionwise module-limit statement [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], for the finite diagram $(\psi_{\mathrm{et}},0)$, identifies these kernels with a module sheaf and the categorical kernel. Explicitly, the factorization $K_{\mathrm{et}}\to\ker\psi_{\mathrm{et}}$ has at $U$ the bijection induced by $\Gamma(U,u^*i)$; it commutes with restrictions because $i_{\mathrm{et}}$ does, and the inverse bijections commute with restrictions by uniqueness of preimages. It is therefore an isomorphism of module sheaves. Since $K_{\mathrm{et}}$ is quasi-coherent by Step 2, so is $\ker\psi_{\mathrm{et}}$ and thus $\ker\varphi$. The same cited sectionwise-limit statement gives the formula $(\ker\varphi)(U)=\ker\varphi_U$ in the item.
